sanskrit: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kiṁ yaviṣṭho na ājagankim īyate dūtyaṁ kad yad ūcima | na nindima camasaṁ yo mahākulo 'gne bhrātar druṇa id bhūtim ūdima ||
english: What greatest, what youngest came to us? What embassy is sent — what did we say? We do not revile the cup of great lineage; O Agni, brother, we declared prosperity only in the wooden vessel.

sanskrit: ekaṁ camasaṁ caturaḥ kṛṇotana tad vo devā abruvan tad va āgamam | saudhanvanā yady evā kariṣyatha sākaṁ devair yajñiyāso bhaviṣyatha ||
english: Make the one cup into four — so the gods said to you, and so I came to you. O sons of Sudhanvan, if you do this, you shall become worthy of sacrifice together with the gods.

sanskrit: agniṁ dūtam prati yad abravītanāśvaḥ kartvo ratha uteha kartvaḥ | dhenuḥ kartvā yuvaśā kartvā dvā tāni bhrātar anu vaḥ kṛtvy emasi ||
english: When you sent word back to Agni as your messenger: 'A horse is to be fashioned, and a chariot too is to be fashioned here; a cow is to be fashioned, two young animals are to be fashioned' — for those deeds, O brother, we come following after you.

sanskrit: cakṛvāṁsa ṛbhavas tad apṛcchata kved abhūd yaḥ sya dūto na ājaganyadāvākhyac camasāñ caturaḥ kṛtān ād it tvaṣṭā gnāsv antar ny ānaje ||
english: Having accomplished that, the Ṛbhus inquired: 'Where then has he gone who came to us as messenger?' When he had reported that the four cups were fashioned, Tvaṣṭṛ straightway hid himself among the women.

sanskrit: hanāmainām̐ iti tvaṣṭā yad abravīc camasaṁ ye devapānam anindiṣuḥ | anyā nāmāni kṛṇvate sute sacām̐ anyair enān kanyā3 nāmabhiḥ sparat ||
english: When Tvaṣṭṛ said 'Let us strike them down' — those who found no fault with the cup for the gods' drinking — they give them other names at the pressing; a young woman contended with them using other names.

sanskrit: indro harī yuyuje aśvinā ratham bṛhaspatir viśvarūpām upājata | ṛbhur vibhvā vājo devām̐ agacchata svapaso yajñiyam bhāgam aitana ||
english: Indra yoked his two bay horses; the Aśvins took possession of a chariot of all forms; Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, and Vāja went to the gods. You who are skilled workers came to a sacrificial share.

sanskrit: niś carmaṇo gām ariṇīta dhītibhir yā jarantā yuvaśā tākṛṇotana | saudhanvanā aśvād aśvam atakṣata yuktvā ratham upa devām̐ ayātana ||
english: With your thoughts you released the cow from her hide; you who made two old ones young again — O sons of Sudhanvan, from the horse you fashioned a horse; having yoked a chariot you drove up to the gods.

sanskrit: idam udakam pibatety abravītanedaṁ vā ghā pibatā muñjanejanaṁ | saudhanvanā yadi tan neva haryatha tṛtīye ghā savane mādayādhvai ||
english: 'Drink this water' — so they said to you — 'or drink this water used for washing the muñja-grass.' O sons of Sudhanvan, if you do not desire that, then be made glad at the third pressing.

sanskrit: āpo bhūyiṣṭhā ity eko abravīd agnir bhūyiṣṭha ity anyo abravīt | vadharyanttīm bahubhyaḥ praiko abravīd ṛtā vadantaś camasām̐ apiṁśata ||
english: One said: 'Water is the greatest'; another said: 'Fire is the greatest'; one spoke out to the many: 'She who hurls the weapon' — speaking truthfully, they fashioned the cups.

sanskrit: śroṇām eka udakaṁ gām avājati māṁsam ekaḥ piṁśati sūnayābhṛtam | ā nimrucaḥ śakṛd eko apābharat kiṁ svit putrebhyaḥ pitarā upāvatuḥ ||
english: One drives water to the lame cow; one shapes meat brought by the slaughter-knife; one carried dung up from the valley at sunset. What indeed did the two parents bestow upon their sons?

sanskrit: udvatsv asmā akṛṇotanā tṛṇaṁ nivatsv apaḥ svapasyayā naraḥ | agohyasya yad asastanā gṛhe tad adyedam ṛbhavo nānu gacchatha ||
english: In the upland pastures, O men of skill, you made grass for him; in the lower pastures, water. That which you fashioned in the house of Agohya who cannot be hidden — that today, O Ṛbhus, you do not follow after.

sanskrit: sammīlya yad bhuvanā paryasarpata kva svit tātyā pitarā va āsatuḥ | aśapata yaḥ karasnaṁ va ādade yaḥ prābravīt pro tasmā abravītana ||
english: When you crept around through the worlds lying still — where indeed did your two ancient parents sit? He who took away the stump of your hand cursed you; who spoke out to him? Tell him that.

sanskrit: suṣupvāṁsa ṛbhavas tad apṛchatāgohya ka idaṁ no abūbudhat | śvānam baṣṭo bodhayi tāram abravīt saṁvatsara idam adyā vy akhyata ||
english: The Ṛbhus who had been sleeping then asked: 'O Agohya, who has awakened us?' A goat said to a dog, its awakener: 'The year — today it has looked upon this thing.'

sanskrit: divā yānti maruto bhūmyāgnir ayaṁ vāto antarikṣeṇa yāti | adbhir yāti varuṇaḥ samudrair yuṣmām̐ icchantaḥ śavaso napātaḥ ||
english: The Maruts travel by day, Agni by earth, this wind travels through the atmosphere; Varuṇa travels with the waters, with the seas — the sons of Strength, seeking you.

sanskrit: mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyur indra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan | yad vājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ||
english: May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts not look askance at us, when we proclaim at the assembly the heroic deeds of the divine-born swift horse.

sanskrit: yan nirṇijā rekṇasā prāvṛtasya rātiṁ gṛbhītām mukhato nayanti | suprāṅ ajo memyad viśvarūpa indrāpūṣṇoḥ priyam apy eti pāthaḥ ||
english: When they lead forward the gift of the one clothed in ornamental garment with golden trappings, seized by the mouth — the well-formed goat bleats, of all forms, and attains the dear portion of Indra and Pūṣan.

sanskrit: eṣa cchāgaḥ puro aśvena vājinā pūṣṇo bhāgo nīyate viśvadevyaḥ | abhipriyaṁ yat puroḻāśam arvatā tvaṣṭed enaṁ sauśravasāya jinvati ||
english: This goat, led forward before the swift horse, is the share of Pūṣan to be offered to all the gods. Tvaṣṭṛ quickens this one along with the horse toward the dear fore-offering cake, for the sake of good fame.

sanskrit: yad dhaviṣyam ṛtuśo devayānaṁ trir mānuṣāḥ pary aśvaṁ nayanti | atrā pūṣṇaḥ prathamo bhāga eti yajñaṁ devebhyaḥ prativedayann ajaḥ ||
english: When men lead the horse around thrice in order at the proper season on the god-directed path of the oblation, Pūṣan's first share comes here, as the goat announces the sacrifice to the gods.

sanskrit: hotādhvaryur āvayā agnimindho grāvagrāba uta śaṁstā suvipraḥ | tena yajñena svaraṁkṛtena sviṣṭena vakṣaṇā ā pṛṇadhvam ||
english: The hotr̥, the adhvaryu, the āvayā, the fire-kindler, the stone-presser, and also the eloquent reciter — fill the flanks through that sacrifice, well-made with its own proper sound, properly offered.

sanskrit: yūpavra skā uta ye yūpavāhāś caṣālaṁ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati | ye cārvate pacanaṁ sambharanty uto teṣām abhigūrtir na invatu ||
english: Those who cut the sacrificial post and those who carry the post, and those who carve the ring for the horse's post, and those who bring together the cooking for the horse — may our praise song also stir them.

sanskrit: upa prāgāt suman me 'dhāyi manma devānām āśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ | anv enaṁ viprā ṛṣayo madanti devānāṁ puṣṭe cakṛmā subandhum ||
english: He came forward, one who has found my hymn good was placed — with back bared — meeting the expectation of the gods; the inspired seer-poets rejoice after him. In the flourishing of the gods we have made a close friend.

sanskrit: yad vājino dāma saṁdānam arvato yā śīrṣaṇyā raśanā rajjur asya | yad vā ghāsya prabhṛtam āsye3 tṛṇaṁ sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
english: The tethering rope, the binding cord of the swift horse, the head-rope, the halter-cord — and whatever bundle of grass has been placed in his mouth — let all that be yours among the gods.

sanskrit: yad aśvasya kraviṣo makṣikāśa yad vā svarau svadhitau riptam asti | yad dhastayoḥ śamitur yan nakheṣu sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
english: Whatever flies have settled on the raw flesh of the horse, whatever clings to the axe or to the cleaver, whatever is on the hands of the slaughterer, whatever on his nails — let all that be yours among the gods.

sanskrit: yad ūvadhyam udarasyāpavāti ya āmasya kraviṣo gandho asti | sukṛtā tac chamiṭāraḥ kṛṇvanty uta medhaṁ śṛtapākam pacantu ||
english: Whatever flows out from the belly as excrement, whatever is the smell of the raw flesh — let the slaughterers make that good; let them cook the sacrificial flesh to proper ripeness.

sanskrit: yat te gātrād agninā pacyamānād abhi śūlaṁ nihatasya avādhāvati | mā tad bhūmyām ā śriṣan mā tṛṇeṣu devebhas tad uśadbhyo rātam astu ||
english: Whatever of your body, roasted by fire, drips down upon the spit of the slain one — may that not cling to the earth, may it not cling to the grass; let it be offered to the gods who desire it.

sanskrit: ye vājinam paripaśyanti pakvaṁ ya īm āhuḥ surabhir nir hareti | ye cārvato māṁsabhikṣām upāsata uto teṣām abhigūrtir na invatu ||
english: Those who watch over the cooked horse, those who say 'carry it out, it is fragrant,' and those who await the distribution of the horse's meat — may our praise also stir them.

sanskrit: yan nīkṣaṇam māṁspacanyā ukhāyā yā pātrāṇi yūṣṇa āsecanāni | ūṣmaṇyāpidhānā carūṇām aṅkāḥ sūnāḥ pari bhūṣanty aśvam ||
english: The hook for the flesh-cooking vessel, the vessels for pouring the broth, the steam-lids of the cauldrons, the hooks — the butchers adorn the horse with all these.

sanskrit: nikramaṇaṁ niṣadanaṁ vivartanaṁ yac ca paḍbīśam arvataḥ | yac ca papau yac ca ghāsiṁ jaghāsa sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
english: The stepping forth, the sitting down, the rolling over, and the hobble of the horse, and whatever he drank, and whatever grass he ate — let all that be yours among the gods.

sanskrit: mā tvā tapat priya ātmāpiyantaṁ mokhā bhrājantya abhi vikta jaghrīḥ | iṣṭaṁ vītam abhigūrtaṁ vaṣaṭkṛtaṁ taṁ devāsaḥ prati gṛbhṇanty aśvam ||
english: Let not the fire that blazes brightly singe you while you come near to your dear self; let not the axe remain in your body. The gods receive that horse who has been offered, presented, praised, and consecrated with the vaṣaṭ-call.

sanskrit: yad aśvāya vāsa upastṛṇanty adhīvāsaṁ yā hiraṇyāny asmai | saṁdānam arvantam paḍbīśam priyā deveṣv ā yāmayanti ||
english: The garment they spread for the horse as a covering, the overgarment, the golden trappings for him — they cause the beloved, tethered, hobbled horse to proceed to the gods.

sanskrit: yat te sāde mahasā śūkṛtasya pārṣṇyā vā kaśayā vā tutoda | srucev a tā haviṣo adhvareṣu sarvā tā te brahmaṇā sūdayāmi ||
english: Whatever struck you in your seat of pride with the heel or with the whip — all those as if the sacrificial ladle at offerings I set aright for you with the sacred word.

sanskrit: catustrimśad vājino devabandhor vaṅkrīr aśvasya svadhitiḥ sam eti | acchidrā gātrā vayunā kṛṇota paruṣ-parur anughuṣyā vi śasta ||
english: Thirty-four ribs of the horse belonging to the gods — the axe comes together with them. Keep the limbs uncut with skill; cut them apart joint by joint, calling out to each.

sanskrit: ekas tvaṣṭur aśvasyā viśastā dvā yantārā bhavatas tathā ṛtuḥ | yā te gātrāṇām ṛtuthā kṛṇomi tā-tā piṇḍānāṁ pra juhomy agnau ||
english: One is the carver of Tvaṣṭṛ's horse; two are the holders — such is the rule. Whatever portions I make in their proper order from your limbs, those portions one by one I offer into the fire.

sanskrit: mā tvā tapat priya ātmāpiyantaṁ mā svadhitis tanva1 ā tiṣṭhipat te | mā te gṛdhnur aviśastātihāya chidrā gātrāṇy asinā mithū kaḥ ||
english: Let not the fire singe you as you draw near to your dear self; let not the axe remain fixed in your body; let not the greedy unskilled cutter, making a mistake, mar your limbs with the knife.

sanskrit: na vā u etan mriyase na riṣyasi devām̐ id eṣi pathibhiḥ sugebhiḥ | harī te yuñjā pṛṣatī abhūtām upāsthād vājī dhuri rāsabhasya ||
english: You do not truly die here, nor are you harmed — you go to the gods by easy paths. The two bays become your yoke-mates, the dappled mares; the swift horse has stood beside the shaft of the donkey.

sanskrit: sugavyaṁ no vājī svaśvyam puṁsaḥ putrām̐ uta viśvāpuṣaṁ rayim | anāgāstvaṁ no aditiḥ kṛṇotu kṣatraṁ no aśvo vanatāṁ haviṣmān ||
english: May the swift horse bring us good cattle and good horses, male offspring, and wealth nourishing all; may Aditi make us guiltless; may the horse bearing the oblation win lordship for us.

sanskrit: yad akrandaḥ prathamaṁ jāyamāna udyan samudrād uta vā purīṣāt | śyenasya pakṣā hariṇasya bāhū upastutya mahi jātaṁ te arvan ||
english: When you cried out first, being born, rising from the ocean or from the earthy matter — the wings of an eagle, the arms of a deer — great is your birth, O swift horse, worthy of praise.

sanskrit: yamena dattaṁ trita enam āyunag indra eṇam prathaamo adhy atiṣṭhat | gandharvo asya raśanām agṛbhṇāt sūrād aśvaṁ vasavo nir ataṣṭa ||
english: Given by Yama, Trita harnessed him; Indra was the first to mount him; the Gandharva grasped his rein. From the sun you fashioned the horse, O Vasus.

sanskrit: asi yamo asy ādityo arvan nasi trito guhyena vrateṇa | asi somena samayā vipṛkta āhus te trīṇi divi bandhanāni ||
english: You are Yama, you are Āditya, O swift horse; you are Trita by your secret ordinance; you are separated from Soma in like manner. They say you have three bonds in heaven.

sanskrit: trīṇi ta āhur divi bandhanāni trīṇy apsu trīṇy antaḥ samudre | uteva me varuṇaś chantsy arvan yatrā ta āhuḥ paramaṁ janitram ||
english: They say you have three bonds in heaven, three in the waters, three within the ocean. To me you seem like Varuṇa, O swift horse, they say your highest birthplace is there.

sanskrit: imā te vājinn avamārjanānīmā śaphānāṁ sanitur nidhānā | atrā te bhadrā raśanā apaśyam ṛtasya yā abhirakṣanti gopāḥ ||
english: These are your cleansing instruments, O vāji; these are the receptacles for the securing of your hooves. Here I saw your good reins, the guardians who protect the cosmic order.

sanskrit: ātmānaṁ te manasāt āt ajānām avo divā patayantam pataṁgam | śiro apaśyam pathibhiḥ sugebhir areṇubhir jehamānam patatri ||
english: I recognized your self from afar with my mind — a bird flying downward from the sky by day. I saw the head, the winged one straining along easy, dustless paths.

sanskrit: atrā te rūpam uttamam apaśyaṁ jigīṣamāṇam iṣa ā pade goḥ | yadā te marto anu bhogam ānaḻ ād id grasiṣṭha oṣadhīr ajīgaḥ ||
english: Here I saw your highest form, striving to win, at the place of the cow's refreshment. When a mortal reached up for your enjoyment, then you seized on the herbs and quickened them.

sanskrit: anu tvā ratho anu maryo arvan anu gāvo 'nu bhagaḥ kanīnām | anu vrātāsas tava sakhyam īyur anu devā mamire vīryaṁ te ||
english: After you came the chariot, after you the warrior, O swift horse; after you the cattle, after you the luck of maidens; after you your bands of companions went to your friendship; after you the gods measured out your heroic power.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaśṛṅgo 'yo asya pādā manoja vā avara indra āsīt | devā id asya haviraadyam āyan yo arvantam prathaamo adhy atiṣṭhat ||
english: Golden-horned, his feet of iron, swift as thought, lower than Indra — the gods came to his oblation-eating, he who first mounted the swift horse.

sanskrit: īrmāntāsaḥ silikamadhyamāsaḥ saṁ śūraṇāso divyāso atyāḥ | haṁsā iva śreṇiśo yatante yad ākṣiṣur divyam ajmam aśvāḥ ||
english: Sweating, with wasp-like waists, the valiant, heavenly swift horses — they strive in line like swans when they have taken the heavenly course.

sanskrit: tava śarīram patayiṣṇv arvan tava cittaṁ vāta iva dhrajīmān | tava śṛṅgāṇi viṣṭhitā puratrāraṇyeṣu jarbhurāṇā caranti ||
english: Your body is eager to fly, O swift horse; your mind rushes along like the wind; your horns scattered in many places wander roaming in the forests.

sanskrit: upa prāgāc chasanaṁ vājy arvā devadṛīcā manasā dīdhyānaḥ | ajaḥ puro nīyate nābhir asyānu paścāt kavayo yanti rebhāḥ ||
english: The swift horse came forward to the slaughter, meditating with god-directed mind. The goat led in front is his navel-cord; behind, the inspired singers go after.

sanskrit: upa prāgāt paramaṁ yat sadastham arvām̐ acchā pitaram mātaraṁ ca | adyā devān juṣṭatamo hi gamyā athā śāste dāśuṣe vāryāṇi ||
english: The swift horse came forward to the highest resting place, toward father and mother. Today he is most pleasing to the gods to go to; then he shall declare desirable gifts to the devout offerer.

sanskrit: asya vāmasya palitasya hotur tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśnaḥ | tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛtapṛṣṭho asyātrāpaśyaṁ viśpatiṁ saptaputram ||
english: Of this beautiful gray hotr̥, his middle brother is the devourer; the third brother, ghee-backed, is this one's. There I saw the lord of the settlement with seven sons.

sanskrit: sapta yuñjanti ratham ekacakram eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā | trinābhi cakram ajaram anarvaṁ yatre mā viśvā bhuvanādhi tasthuḥ ||
english: Seven yoke the single-wheeled chariot; one horse with seven names draws it. The wheel is three-hubbed, imperishable, not worn out — on it all these worlds stand.

sanskrit: imaṁ ratham adhi ye sapta tasthuḥ saptacakraṁ sapta vahanty aśvāḥ | sapta svasāro abhi saṁ navante yatra gavāṁ nihitā sapta nāma ||
english: The seven who stand on this seven-wheeled chariot — seven horses draw it. Seven sisters call out together, where the seven names of the cattle are set down.

sanskrit: ko dadarśa prathamaṁ jāyamānam asthanvantaṁ yad anasthā bibharti | bhūmyā asur asṛg ātmā kva svit ko vidvāṁsam upa gāt praṣṭum etat ||
english: Who saw the one being born first, the one with bones, which the boneless one bears? The earth's vital breath, blood, and soul — where are they? Who has gone to the wise one to ask this?

sanskrit: pākaḥ pṛcchāmi manasāvijānan devānām enā nihitā padāni | vatse baṣkaye 'dhi sapta tantūn vi tatnire kavaya otavā u ||
english: Childlike I ask, not knowing in my mind — what are the hidden tracks of the gods there? The poets have stretched out, as if for weaving, seven threads upon the young calf — so they say.

sanskrit: acikitvāñ cikituṣaś cid atra kavīn pṛcchāmi vidmane na vidvān | vi yas tastambha ṣaḻ imā rajāṁsy ajasya rūpe kim api svid ekam ||
english: Not knowing, even among the knowing, I ask the poet-seers here for the sake of knowledge, I who do not know — what is the one thing that in the form of the unborn has propped up these six spaces apart?

sanskrit: iha bravītu ya īm aṅga vedāsya vāmasya nihitam padaṁ veḥ | śīrṣṇaḥ kṣīraṁ duhrate gāvo asya vavrī vasānā udakam padāpuḥ ||
english: Let him speak here who truly knows the hidden track of this lovely bird. The cows milk milk from his head; clothed in wrappings they have drunk water with their feet.

sanskrit: mātā pitaram ṛta ā babhāja dhīty agre manasā saṁ hi jagme | sā bībhatsur garbharasā nividdh ā namasvanta id upavākam īyuḥ ||
english: The mother apportioned the father through the cosmic order; at the beginning of thought she met him with her mind. She, full of desire, with embryo-essence laid in her, the reverential ones went to the invocation.

sanskrit: yuktā mātāsīd dhuri dakṣiṇāyā atiṣṭhad garbho vṛjanīṣv antaḥ | amīmed vatso anu gām apaśyad viśvarūpyaṁ triṣu yojaneṣu ||
english: The mother was yoked to the right-hand shaft; the embryo stood within the enclosures. The calf lowed; it saw the cow in pursuit of all-encompassing forms in the three yokings.

sanskrit: tisro mātṝs trīn pitṝn bibhrad eka ūrdhvas tasthau nem ava glāpayanti | mantrayante divo amuṣya pṛṣṭhe viśvavidaṁ vācam aviśvaminvām ||
english: Bearing three mothers and three fathers, the one stood upright — they do not weaken it below. On the back of that heaven they confer, speaking the all-knowing speech that not all know.

sanskrit: dvādaśāraṁ nahi taj jarāya varvati cakram pari dyām ṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithuṇāso atra sapta śatāni viṁśatiś ca tasthuḥ ||
english: The twelve-spoked wheel of the cosmic order rolls round the sky and does not decay — on it, O Agni, stand paired children, seven hundred and twenty.

sanskrit: pañcapādam pitaraṁ dvādaśākṛtiṁ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇam | athe me anya upare vicakṣaṇaṁ saptacakre ṣaḻara āhur arpitam ||
english: The five-footed father with twelve forms they call the bountiful one in the upper half of the sky. But others here say of the far-seer standing below that he is set upon a seven-wheeled, six-spoked wheel.

sanskrit: pañcāre cakre parivartamāne tasmin ā tasthu r bhuvanāni viśvā | tasya nākṣas tapyate bhūribhāraḥ sanād eva na śīryate sanābhiḥ ||
english: On the five-spoked wheel revolving all the worlds have taken their stand. Its axle is not heated though it bears a great load. From the ancient time the hub does not break.

sanskrit: sanemi cakram ajaram vi vāvṛta uttānāyāṁ daśa yuktā vahanti | sūryasya cakṣū rajasaity āvṛtaṁ tasmin ārpitā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: The wheel with complete rim, ageless, revolves; ten yoked ones draw it on the outstretched path. The sun's eye moves enveloped in the mist; on it all worlds are set.

sanskrit: sākaṁjānāṁ saptaṭham āhur ekajaṁ ṣaḻ id yamā ṛṣayo devajā iti | teṣām iṣṭāni vihitāni dhāmaśaḥ sthātre rejante vikṛtāni rūpaśaḥ ||
english: The seventh of the simultaneous-born they call the only-born; six are the twin-born seers, born of the gods they say. Their desires are laid out in the habitations; they who stand firm vibrate in changing forms.

sanskrit: striyaḥ satīs tām̐ u me puṁsa āhuḥ paśyad akṣaṇvān na vi cetad andhaḥ | kavir yaḥ putraḥ sa īm ā ciketa yas tā vijānāt sa pituṣ pitāsat ||
english: They are females, yet the knowing ones call them males — one who has eyes and looks sees it; the blind one does not discern it. The son who is a seer has understood them; he who knows them would be the father of his father.

sanskrit: avaḥ pareṇa para enāvareṇa padā vatsam bibhratī gaur ud asthāt | sā kadrīcī kaṁ svid ardhaṁ parāgāt kva svit sūte nahi yūthe antaḥ ||
english: Below the upper and above the lower, the cow has stood up bearing the calf on her feet. Toward which half has she gone away? Where does she give birth? Surely not within the herd.

sanskrit: avaḥ pareṇa pitaraṁ yo asyānuveda para enāvareṇa | kavīyamānaḥ ka iha pra vocad devaṁ manaḥ kuto adhi prajātam ||
english: Whoever knows the father — above the lower and below the upper — who here acting as a seer might proclaim the divine mind from whence it was born?

sanskrit: ye arvāñcas tām̐ u parāca āhur ye parāñcas tām̐ u arvāca āhuḥ | indraś ca yā cakrathuḥ soma tāni dhurā na yuktā rajaso vahanti ||
english: Those who face this way they call those who face away; those who face away they call those who face this way. Indra and Soma — those things you two have made, yoked to the shaft, carry the atmospheric space.

sanskrit: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṁ vṛkṣam pari ṣasvajāte | tayor anyaḥ pippalaṁ svādv atty anaśnann anyo abhi cākaśīti ||
english: Two eagles of beautiful wings, companions and friends, clasp the same tree. One of the two eats the sweet fig; the other, not eating, looks on.

sanskrit: yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgam animeṣaṁ vidathābhisvaranti | ino viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ sa mādhīraḥ pākam atrā viveśa ||
english: Where the eagles unblinkingly chant their portion of immortality in the assembly — the master, the guardian of the whole world, the wise one — has entered the simple one there.

sanskrit: yasmin vṛkṣe madhvadaḥ suparṇā niviśante suvate cādhi viśve | tasyed āhuḥ pippalaṁ svādv agre tan non naśad yaḥ pitaraṁ na veda ||
english: On the tree where the honey-eating eagles make their home and give birth, the whole world is above — they say the sweet fig is at the top; he will not reach it who does not know the Father.

sanskrit: yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitaṁ traiṣṭubhād vā traiṣṭubhaṁ niratakṣata | yad vā jagaj jagatyāhitam padaṁ ya it tad vidus te amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||
english: What is set in the gāyatrī beyond the gāyatrī, what they fashioned in the triṣṭubh beyond the triṣṭubh, what is the step set in the jagatī beyond the jagatī — those who know that have attained immortality.

sanskrit: gāyatreṇa prati mimīte arkami arkeṇa sāma traiṣṭubhena vākam | vākena vākaṁ dvipadā catuṣpadākṣareṇa mimate sapta vāṇīḥ ||
english: With the gāyatrī he measures out the sacred song; with the song, the sāman; with the triṣṭubh, the vāk. With speech he measures speech, two-footed and four-footed; with the syllable they measure the seven vāṇīs.

sanskrit: jagatā sindhum divy astabhāyad rathantare sūryam pary apaśyat | gāyatrasya samidhas tisra āhus tato mahnā pra ririce mahitvā ||
english: With the jagatī he propped up the river in the sky; in the rathantara he beheld the sun round about. They say the gāyatra has three fuel-sticks; from that it has surpassed all in greatness by its greatness.

sanskrit: upa hvaye sudughāṁ dhenum etāṁ suhasto godhug uta dodad enām | śreṣṭhaṁ savaṁ savitā sāviṣan no 'bhīddho gharmas tad u ṣu pra vocam ||
english: I call hither this good-milking cow; a skillful hand should milk her and urge her on. May Savitṛ impel the best impulsion for us; the heated cauldron ablaze — that I now declare.

sanskrit: hiṅkṛṇvatī vasupatnī vasūnāṁ vatsam icchantī manasābhy āgāt | duhām aśvibhyām payo aghnyeyaṁ sā vardhatām mahate saubhagāya ||
english: The cow, lady of treasures, making the hiṅ sound, came in her mind seeking the calf. Let this inviolable one be milked for the two Aśvins; may she thrive for great good fortune.

sanskrit: gaur amīmed anu vatsam miṣantam mūrdhānam hiṅṅ akṛṇon mātavā u | sṛkvāṇaṁ gharmam abhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyum payate payobhiḥ ||
english: The cow lowed after the calf gazing at her; she made the hiṅ sound at the head, in her maternal desire. Lowing for the seething pot with parted lips, she measures out her might with streams of milk.

sanskrit: ayaṁ sa śiṅkte yena gaur abhīvṛtā mimāti māyuṁ dhvasanāv adhi śritā | sā cittibhir ni hi cakāra martyaṁ vidyud bhavantī prati vavrim auhata ||
english: This is the one that bellows, by whom the cow surrounded lows its call, resting on the two nostrils. She by her powers has laid the mortal low; becoming lightning she has pushed aside the covering.

sanskrit: anac chaye turagātu jīvam ejad dhruvaṁ madhya ā pastyānām | jīvo mṛtasya carati svadhābhir amartyo martyenā sayoniḥ ||
english: The breathing one lies down; the fleet-moving living one stirs about the firm one in the middle of the settlements. The living one wanders among the dead by its own powers — the immortal one, of the same womb as the mortal.

sanskrit: apaśyaṁ gopām anipadyamānam ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carantam | sa sadhrīcīḥ sa viṣūcīr vasāna ā varīvarti bhuvaneṣv antaḥ ||
english: I saw the herdsman who does not dismount, going along the paths hither and thither. He, clothing himself in converging and diverging forms, moves round and round within the worlds.

sanskrit: ya īm cakāra na so asya veda ya īm dadarśa hirug in nu tasmāt | sa mātur yonā parivīto antar bahuprajā nirṛtim ā viveśa ||
english: He who made it does not know it; he who saw it — from him it conceals itself. Enclosed within his mother's womb, he who has many offspring has entered into dissolution.

sanskrit: dyaur me pitā janitā nābhir atra bandhu r me mātā pṛthivī mahīyam | utānayoś camvo3r yonir antar atrā pitā duhitur garbham ādhāt ||
english: Heaven is my father, my begetter; the navel is here; this great earth is my mother, my kin. Between the two spread bowls is the womb; here the father placed the embryo in the daughter.

sanskrit: pṛcchāmi tvā paraṁ antam pṛthivyāḥ pṛcchāmi yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ | pṛcchāmi tvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ pṛcchāmi vācaḥ paramaṁ vyoma ||
english: I ask you about the furthest end of the earth; I ask where is the navel of the world; I ask you about the seed of the vigorous horse; I ask about the highest heaven of speech.

sanskrit: iyaṁ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṁ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ | ayaṁ somo vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto brahmāyaṁ vācaḥ paramaṁ vyoma ||
english: This altar-ground is the furthest end of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world; this Soma is the seed of the vigorous horse; this brahman priest is the highest heaven of speech.

sanskrit: saptārdha garbhā bhuvanasya reto viṣṇos tiṣṭhanti pradiśā vidharmaṇi | te dhītibhir manasā te vipaścitaḥ paribhuvaḥ pari bhavanti viśvataḥ ||
english: The seven half-embryos, the seed of the world, stand by the ordinances in the domains of Viṣṇu's far-spreading. Those wise and thoughtful ones, encompassing beings, surround everything on all sides.

sanskrit: na vi jānāmi yad ive dam asmi niṇyaḥ saṁnaddho manasā carāmi | yadā māgan prathamajā ṛtasyād id vāco aśnuve bhāgam asyāḥ ||
english: I do not know what this thing is that I am — bound in mystery, I wander with my mind. When the firstborn of the cosmic order came to me, then I attained a share of this speech.

sanskrit: apāṅ prāṅ eti svadhayā gṛbhīto 'martyo martyenā sayoniḥ | tā śaśvantā viṣūcīnā viyantā ny anyaṁ cikyur na ni cikyur anyam ||
english: Going backward and forward, seized by his own power, the immortal of the same womb as the mortal — the two, moving perpetually apart in different directions, have perceived the one, have not perceived the other.

sanskrit: ṛco akṣare parame vyoman yasmin devā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ | yas tan na veda kim ṛcā kariṣyati ya it tad vidus ta ime sam āsate ||
english: In the imperishable highest heaven in which all the gods have taken their seat — what will he do with the ṛc who does not know that? Only those who know it are seated here together.

sanskrit: sūyavasād bhagatī hi bhūyā atho vayam bhagatantaḥ syāma | addi tṛṇam aghnye viśvadānīm piba śuddham udakam ācarantī ||
english: May you be blessed with good pasture; may we too be blessed. Eat grass, O inviolable one, ever and always; drink pure water as you go about.

sanskrit: gaurīr mimāya salilāni takṣaty ekapadī dvipadī sā catuṣpadī | aṣṭāpadī navapadī babhūvuṣī sahasrākṣarā parame vyoman ||
english: The shining cow shaped waters, crafting them — she who is one-footed, two-footed, four-footed; she who has become eight-footed, nine-footed, possessing a thousand syllables in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti tena jīvanti pradiśaś catasraḥ | tataḥ kṣaraty akṣaraṁ tad viśvam upa jīvati ||
english: From her the seas flow forth in all directions; by her the four quarters live. From her flows the syllable, on that the whole world lives.

sanskrit: śakamayaṁ dhūmam ārād apaśyaṁ viṣūvatā para enāvareṇa | ukṣāṇam pṛśnim apacanta vīrās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan ||
english: From afar I saw a dung-smoky cloud rising at the equinox, above the lower and below the upper. The heroes cooked the dappled bull; these were the first ordinances.

sanskrit: traya ḥ keśina ṛtuthā vi cakṣate saṁvatsare vapata eka eṣām | viśvam eko abhi caṣṭe śacībhir dhrājir ekasya dadṛśe na rūpam ||
english: Three long-haired ones reveal themselves in order at the proper season; one of them shaves at the year's end; one gazes over the whole world with his powers; of one the rushing is seen but not the form.

sanskrit: catvāri vāk parimitā padāni tāni vidur brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ | guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṁ vāco manuṣyā vadanti ||
english: Speech is measured out in four quarters; the wise Brāhmaṇas know them. Three are placed in secret and do not stir; of speech, humans speak only the fourth.

sanskrit: indram mitraṁ varuṇam agnim āhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṁ sad viprā bahudhā vadanty agniṁ yamam mātariśvānam āhuḥ ||
english: They call it Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and it is the divine, winged Garutmān. The one being the seers speak of in many ways: they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaṁ niyānaṁ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divam ut patanti | ta āvavṛtran sadanād ṛtasyād id ghṛtena pṛthivī vy udyate ||
english: Golden-hued eagles, wearing the waters, fly upward to the black track in the sky. They have returned from the seat of the cosmic order; then the earth is spread out with ghee.

sanskrit: dvādaśa pradhayaś cakram ekaṁ trīṇi nabhyāni ka u tac ciketa | tasmin sākaṁ triśatā na śaṅkavo 'rpitāḥ ṣaṣṭir na calācalāsaḥ ||
english: Twelve fellies, one wheel, three hubs — who has understood that? On it are set together three hundred pins and sixty, and they do not budge.

sanskrit: yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi | yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ sarasvatī tam iha dhātave kaḥ ||
english: O Sarasvatī, that breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which bestows well-being, with which you nourish all desirable things — the treasure-bearing, wealth-finding, generous one — bring that here for us to drink.

sanskrit: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan | te ha nākaṁ mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ||
english: The gods worshipped sacrifice with sacrifice; those were the first ordinances. These great ones have attained the vault of heaven where the ancient Sādhya gods are.

sanskrit: samānam etad udakam uc caity ava cāhabhiḥ | bhūmim parjanyā jinvanti divaṁ jinvanty agnayaḥ ||
english: This same water rises up and comes back down by days; the rains quicken the earth; the fires quicken the sky.

sanskrit: divyaṁ suparṇaṁ vāyasaṁ bṛhantam apāṁ garbhaṁ darśatam oṣadhīnām | abhīpato vṛṣṭibhis tarpayantaṁ sarasvantam avase johavīmi ||
english: The heavenly eagle, the great bird of the sky, the embryo of the waters, the shining one of herbs — Sarasvan who refreshes those who desire him with his rains — I call him with repeated calls for help.

sanskrit: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḻāḥ samānyā marutaḥ sam mimikṣuḥ | kayā matī kuta etāsa ete 'rcanti śuṣmaṁ vṛṣaṇo vasūyā ||
english: By what splendor have the Maruts, of equal age, of the same nest, of the same band, mingled together? By what thought, from where have these come — the vigorous ones who sing their strength, desiring riches?

sanskrit: kasya brahmāṇi jujuṣur yuvānaḥ ko adhvare maruta ā vavarta | śyenām̐ iva dhrajato antarikṣe kena mahā manasā rīramāma ||
english: Whose sacred formulations have the young ones delighted in? Who has turned the Maruts to the sacrifice? Like swift hawks through the atmosphere — by what great thought shall we find pleasure together?

sanskrit: kutas tvam indra māhinaḥ sann eko yāsi satpate kiṁ ta itthā | sam pṛcchase samarāṇaḥ śubhānair voces tan no harivo yat te asme ||
english: O Indra, being great, why do you go alone, O lord of the good? What then is your purpose? Meeting together equally with the splendid ones — declare to us what you have for us, O one with the bay horses.

sanskrit: brahmāṇi me matayaḥ śaṁ sutāsaḥ śuṣma iyarti prabhṛto me adriḥ | ā śāsate prati haryanty ukthemā harī vahattas tā no accha ||
english: My sacred formulations and thoughts are potent; the pressed stone sets my strength in motion. The recitations summon, the hymns come back in answer — let these two bay horses carry you here to us.

sanskrit: ato vayam antamebhir yujānāḥ svakṣetrebhis tanvaḥ śumbhamānāḥ | mahobhir etām̐ upa yujmahe nv indra svadhām anu hi no babhūtha ||
english: For this reason we, joined with our nearest companions, adorning our bodies with our own domains, now yoke these with our great powers. O Indra, you have indeed become for us according to our own nature.

sanskrit: kva1 syā vo marutaḥ svadhāsīd yan mām ekaṁ samadha ttāhihatye | ahaṁ hy ugras taviṣas tuviṣmān viśvasya śatror anamaṁ vadhasnaiḥ ||
english: Where was your solidarity, O Maruts, when you left me alone in the serpent-slaying? For I am the fierce, mighty, powerful one; I have crushed every foe with my weapons.

sanskrit: bhūri cakartha yujyebhir asme samānebhir vṛṣabha pauṁsyebhiḥ | bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭhendra kratvā maruto yad vaśāma ||
english: You have done much for us with our companions, O bull, with the manly powers shared among equals. We shall do many things, O strongest Indra, with resolve, as the Maruts desire.

sanskrit: vadhīṁ vṛtram maruta indiriyeṇa svena bhāmena taviṣo babhūvān | aham etā manave viśvaścandrāḥ sugā apaś cakara vajrabāhuḥ ||
english: I slew Vṛtra, O Maruts, with Indra's power, becoming mighty with my own fury. I the one of bright-all splendors, the thunderbolt-armed, made the waters flow freely for Manu.

sanskrit: anuttam ā te maghavan nakir nu na tvāvām̐ asti devatā vidānaḥ | na jāyamāno naśate na jāto yāni kariṣyā kṛṇuhi pravṛddha ||
english: Your power is unsurpassed, O Maghavan; none now knows a deity like you. Neither one being born can attain you nor one already born; what you will do — do that, O most exalted one.

sanskrit: ekasya cin me vibhv astv ojo yā nu dadhrṣvān kṛṇavai manīṣā | ahaṁ hy ugro maruto vidāno yāni cyavam indra id īśa eṣām ||
english: Let my power be preeminent even alone; what I shall do, I will do with daring thought. For I am the fierce one who knows, O Maruts — of those things I set moving, Indra alone is master.

sanskrit: amandan mā marutaḥ stomo atra yan me naraḥ śrutyam brahma cakra | indrāya vṛṣṇe sumakhāya mahyaṁ sakhye sakhāyas tanve tanūbhiḥ ||
english: The hymn of praise has gladdened me here, O Maruts, that the men made the sacred word worthy of hearing — for me Indra, the bull, the exceedingly good, as friends with their bodies in friendship to my body.

sanskrit: eved ete prati mā rocanānā anedyaḥ śrava eṣo dadhānāḥ | saṁcakṣyā marutaś candravarṇā acchānta me chadayāthā ca nūnam ||
english: Thus these very ones, shining brightly toward me, bearing blameless glory — seeing me, O Maruts, of resplendent forms, shine for me and now give me delight.

sanskrit: ko nv atra maruto māmahe vaḥ pra yātana sakhīm̐r acchā sakhāyaḥ | manmāni citrā apivātayanta eṣāṁ bhūta navedā ma ṛtānām ||
english: Who among these praises you, O Maruts? Go forth toward your friends, O friends. Setting in motion their varied formulations — be for me a knower of the cosmic laws of these.

sanskrit: ā yad duvasyād duvase na kārus asmāñ cakre mānyasya medhā | o ṣu varta maruto vipram acche mā brahmāṇi jaritā vo arcat ||
english: As a poet serves at the call of one who deserves service, the wisdom of the one worthy of honor has made us its own. O Maruts, turn now toward the inspired one; the singer has praised your sacred formulations.

sanskrit: eṣa vaḥ stomo maruta iyaṁ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ | eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṁ vidyāmeṣaṁ vṛjanaṁ jīradānum ||
english: This is your praise-hymn, O Maruts, this is the song of the poet Māndārya, worthy of honor. May this go forth for the body's nourishment; may we find this settled community that gives life swiftly.
